title: Sampling sanity harness and adaptor notes
content:
Purpose and quick summary:

This note collects the design and practical steps for a small, reusable profiling harness we use for CI smoke checks and local triage. The goal is to provide a lightweight, deterministic sampling path + sanitizer so developers can: reproduce noisy token-hotspots, produce reproducible perf.data and flamegraphs, and validate that CI collectors and uploaders are healthy before long-running perf jobs start.

Why this exists (context):
- CI has started to surface intermittent collector failures: missing symbols, truncated stacks, and huge differences between local and CI flames.
- Full load benches are expensive; we need a cheap CI gate (~5–30s) that still exercises the request path and KV cache hot loop for regressing alloc/jitter issues.
- Existing runbooks focused on long traces; this doc is for the compact harness + adaptor tooling used by eng teams for quick iterations.

High-level components (what the harness does):
1) Warmup driver: deterministic request stream (small inputs, seeded RNG) that triggers typical request flow (model forward, kv cache hits).
2) Sampler adaptor: runs perf/ebpf/uprobes depending on environment and normalizes outputs to a common format (perf.data + folded stacks).
3) Sanitizer: strips sensitive path prefixes, maps addresses to container-friendly symbol files, and re-creates a minimal symbol store for CI uploaders.
4) Flame-slicer: converts folded stacks to flamegraph.svg with consistent color palette and annotations for critical hot loops (KV cache, attention_forward, token_emit).
5) Checkpoint collector: saves artifacts to a local artifact dir (perf.data, folded.txt, flame.svg, brief.txt) for both local inspection and CI upload.

When to run this harness:
- Pre-commit: run locally when touching scheduler/kvcache/attention code paths.
- Pre-merge perf gate: CI job will run harness; artifacts get uploaded and small regression thresholds checked (95th p50 token latency).
- Triage: when a long-running perf job shows a regression, use harness to narrow down which micro-op changed.

How to run locally (examples):
- Prereqs: Linux workstation, docker or local build, perf (>=5.4), flamegraph scripts installed (https://github.com/brendangregg/FlameGraph).

Local bash quick-run (containerized):
export HARN_DIR=~/tmp/prof-harness-$(date +%s)
mkdir -p $HARN_DIR/artifacts
docker run --rm --cap-add=sys_admin --cap-add=perf_event -v $PWD:/workspace -v $HARN_DIR/artifacts:/artifacts redwood/serving-debug:latest /workspace/tools/harness/run_harness.sh --mode=perf --duration=20 --out=/artifacts

Local native (no docker):
# build the harness binary: bazel build //tools/harness:run_harness
./bazel-bin/tools/harness/run_harness --mode=perf --duration=20 --out=./artifacts

What the harness emits (artifact list):
- artifacts/perf.data  (raw perf record)
- artifacts/folded.stacks.txt  (perf script | stack collapse output)
- artifacts/flame.svg  (flamegraph)
- artifacts/brief.txt  (p90/p99 token lat summary + top 10 stacks)
- artifacts/symbols.tar.gz (if BUILD_SYMBOLS=true)

Sampler adaptor behavior (notes):
- On CI we prefer perf record -F 99 -g --call-graph dwarf to capture unwinding in containerized builds.
- If perf unavailable (some GKE nodes), we fall back to an eBPF sampler that emits samples every 4ms. A small python adaptor normalizes both outputs to the same folded stack format used by flame-slicer.
- For reproducibility include: --sample-seed <int> to freeze RNG used by the harness driver.

Sanitizer concerns and steps:
- Problem: binary path/version mismatches result in perf script dropping symbols. Sanitizer will: 1) map /workspace checkout path to a stable prefix, 2) drop sensitive env vars embedded in logs, 3) attempt to run eu-stack/syms on artifact and produce a symbols.tar.gz to upload with CI.
- CI note: we do NOT upload raw perf.data to external storage for privacy reasons; instead we upload folded stacks + symbols.tar.gz.

CI job snippets (Jenkins/Buildkite example):
steps:
  - label: "perf-smoke-harness"
    plugins:
      - docker#v3.7.0:
          image: redwood/serving-debug:latest
    commands:
      - export ART_DIR=${BUILDKITE_ARTIFACT_PATH:-/tmp/artifacts}
      - /workspace/tools/harness/run_harness --mode=perf --duration=${DUR:-25} --out=${ART_DIR}
      - tar -czf artifacts.tgz ${ART_DIR}
      - buildkite-agent artifact upload artifacts.tgz
      - ./tools/harness/check_regression.py --baseline baselines/latest.json --artifacts ${ART_DIR} || exit 1

Design choices and rationale (short):
- Keep harness short (20–30s) so it's cheap in CI; sample-rate and warmup tuned to still surface script-level hotspots.
- Normalize outputs early so downstream tooling (flame visualizer, regression checker) can be shared across multiple collection methods.
- Prefer folded stacks for CI (smaller, deterministic) over full perf.data uploads.

Triaging regression workflow (step-by-step):
1) Re-run harness locally with same sample-seed and DUT binary (checkout the exact sha used in failing CI).
2) Compare folded.stacks.txt to baseline (git diff style) — look for new top frames or changed counts.
3) If diff points to unknown symbol names or <unknown> entries, run the sanitizer to rebuild symbols and re-run perf script.
4) If behavior differs widely between local and CI, switch sampler adaptor: try eBPF vs perf to check for unwinding differences.
5) If flame shows increased time in allocation paths (malloc/free, new/delete), run the harness with the memory allocator sanitizer build (MALLOC_PROFILE=1) to capture heap hotspots.

Common pitfalls and mitigation: 
- Large JIT-generated frames: ensure JIT/symbolization is enabled in sanitizer (we snapshot /tmp/jit-syms and map addresses).
- Perf permissions: always run under --cap-add=SYS_ADMIN and ensure perf_event_paranoid <= 1 in container CI images.
- Noisy background tasks in shared CI runners: prefer pinned runner pools for these smoke checks, or add a side-channel metric (cpu steal) to detect noisy runs.

Checklist before opening a perf regression PR:
- [ ] run harness locally with --sample-seed and attach artifacts to PR
- [ ] validate no <unknown> frames in folded.stacks.txt (or include symbols.tar.gz)
- [ ] run ./tools/harness/check_regression.py and confirm no failure or document rationale for accepted change
- [ ] mention baseline commit (sha) and test machine type in PR description

Future improvements (ideas backlog):
- Add a tiny eBPF kernel module to capture precise kernel->user transitions for token-emission hotspots.
- Make harness produce annotated flamegraphs with overlayed token-emission timestamps.
- Add a light-weight sample comparator that highlights function-level delta percentages between two folded stacks.

Notes / open questions: 
- We need to decide if folded stacks alone are sufficient for legal/privacy review when sharing with partners. (ping security)
- Can we reduce the required container capabilities and still get reliable stacks on GKE? (open: infra ticket INFRA-924)

Differs from other docs: this is intentionally compact, pragmatic, and developer-facing: a minimal harness + adaptor approach that prioritizes reproducible small artifacts over long-running traces or full-system profiling playbooks.

Recent runs (examples):
- 2024-09-30: run id harness-20240930-ax1, 20s, top stacks showed 18% increase in attention_forward (linked: JIRA: PERF-317)
- 2024-07-05: run id harness-20240705-local, used eBPF adaptor to validate unwinding differences on kernel 5.15.

Owner notes (Aisha): if you are triaging a perf regression and want help, ping me in #perf-signal and include artifacts tarball + the baseline sha. The harness is intentionally easy to invoke; we should make it the first step in every regression workflow.

TODOs:
- Add explicit CI thresholds file for the harness (JSON) and wire into check_regression.py
- Add a short README in tools/harness explaining symbol build steps for macOS devs
- Explore replacing perf script folding step with a Rust-based fast-fold utility to speed up CI processing
